How fast does **US debt interest**
pile up?

FY25 interest: $970B ÷ 31,536,000 s
Pay: BLS median $1,251 a week × 52

vo.text: $970 billion a year, split into seconds.
And none of it pays the debt down.

data.label: US debt interest, since you hit play

notes: Rate: FY2025 net interest $970,000,000,000 ÷ 31,536,000 s (365 days) = $30,758.498 a second (perSecond 30,758.50; shown ≈ $30,800). Per hour: 30,758.498 × 3,600 = $110,730,594 ≈ $111 million. Counter 0-32.9 s: 30,758.498 × 32.9 = 1,011,954.59 → ≈ $1,011,955. Passes (value ÷ rate): average new car $50,089 (KBB average new-vehicle transaction price, Aug 2026, Cox Automotive 2026-09-10) at 1.628 s; median new house $393,700 (Census/HUD New Residential Sales, Aug 2026) at 12.800 s; 10 years of median pay $1,251 × 52 × 10 = $650,520 (BLS usual weekly earnings, Q2 2026, USDL-26-1257) at 21.149 s; $1,000,000 at 32.511 s (≈ 33 seconds). Inputs as verified in teasers/v2/10-cost-counter.md (net interest, pay, house) and teasers/v2/08-unit-ladder.md (KBB). Interest is the cost of carrying the debt; none of it repays principal.
